A 41-year-old male presents to the primary care clinic with a one-year history of progressive exertional
dyspnea and a dry cough. His occupational history includes aerospace engineering, coal mining, and
sandblasting over the past 30 years. Vital signs are as follows: temperature 36.8 ºC (98.2 ºF), blood
pressure 125/68 mmHg, respiratory rate 13/min, pulse 86/min, and oxygen saturation 94% on room air.
Physical examination reveals normal heart sounds on auscultation and fine inspiratory crackles
bilaterally without wheezes or rhonchi. There is no finger clubbing. Given the patient’s exposure
history, pneumoconiosis is suspected. Which diagnostic test would best help distinguish between the
different types of pneumoconiosis? Answer Choices: (A) V/Q scan (B) High-resolution CT (HRCT) with
inspiratory and expiratory views (C) Bronchoalveolar lavage (D) Computed tomography (CT) imaging
of the chest (E) Pulmonary function testing with spirometry (F) Serum ACE level measurement (G)
Diffusing capacity of the lungs for carbon monoxide (DLCO) measurement (H) Lung biopsy with
histopathological examination (I) Sputum cytology for asbestos or silica particles (J) FEV1/FVC ratio
measurement
 A. Bronchoalveolar lavage
B. V/Q scan

C. Diffusing capacity of the lungs for carbon monoxide (DLCO) measurement
D. Pulmonary function testing with spirometry
E. Serum ACE level measurement
F. Sputum cytology for asbestos or silica particles
G. Computed tomography (CT) imaging of the chest
H. Lung biopsy with histopathological examination
I. FEV1/FVC ratio measurement
J. High-resolution CT (HRCT) with inspiratory and expiratory views
